canonical_statement: For every positive real period T and every continuous complex-valued function f on AddCircle T, the arithmetic means of the symmetric Fourier partial sums S_0(f), ..., S_n(f) converge uniformly to f.
domain_and_universes: T : Real with Fact (0 < T); f : C(AddCircle T, Complex); n : Nat; Fourier frequencies j : Int; Prop in Lean universe 0
hypotheses: f is a bundled continuous complex-valued map
conclusion: Tendsto (fejerMean f) atTop (nhds f) in the continuous-map topology, equivalently uniform convergence on compact AddCircle T.

definitions.symmetricFourierPartialSum: sum over Int frequencies j in [-n,n] of fourierCoeff f j scalar-multiplied by fourier j
definitions.fejerMean: (n+1)^(-1) scalar-multiplied by the sum of symmetricFourierPartialSum f k for k in range (n+1)

source_relationship: The repository gloss identifies Fejer's theorem but omits conventions. The selected statement is the standard periodic uniform theorem and agrees with the duplicate metadata record THM-M-0291; this statement artifact supplies no primary-source or human-proof credit.

degenerate_cases: Nonpositive periods are excluded by Fact (0 < T). The index starts at zero; S_0 contains exactly frequency zero and the zeroth Fejer mean is S_0, both kernel-checked. Constant and zero functions remain in scope.
